I was a stage hand for a play some friends were in. We were on stage during rehearsal, loading in the set, and playing some music. Iron and Wine came on, their cover of Such Great Heights. This guy I had been talking to, another stage hand, came over and grabbed my hand and pulled me up off the stage, and right there in front of everyone, under the spotlights, started to slow dance me to that lovely song. I have never forgotten that moment.

Equally romantic, and maybe even more so because I felt so strongly for him, was the time I was out with this man I was utterly, completely insanely crazy about. We were walking home from the bar, and it was bitterly cold and crystal clear. You could see every star. We stopped for a minute so traffic could go by and he told me, "There is nowhere else I would rather be right now than here with you." And he kissed me. And I swear to fucking god, on my grave, at that exact moment this beautiful blue-white shooting star went across the sky right under the moon. I write in a journal a lot. It helps me stay centered, maintain my memory, and work out the relationships in my life. This guy I was seeing was kind of aloof and generally distracted by superficial desires and his own insecurities (we were in college), but was creative and I knew he had a lot of depth he wasn't willing to share on a daily basis. He often held me at arms length but it only made me more intrigued. In short, he was addicting.

At the time of the relationship, I was still writing in this cheesy pink notebook that I'd had since I was 14. For my birthday, he surprised me with a red moleskin (by wrapping it in a scarf) and filled it with pictures of the two of us, of him and I as children, of places we'd been together. And on the first page, he wrote an inscription to me that ended with "I love you," which we hadn't said yet. I melted right into the floor.

The relationship went up in flames (okay more like a nuclear explosion) but I've never received such an incredible, thoughtful, personal gift from anyone since. Sigh.
